coverage.main: Read all nineteen pages of arXiv 1809.02861v4, including references; visually inspected the transfer matrices in Figures 7, 12, 16 and 21 and surrounding captions/setup on PDF pp. 10, 13, 14 and 16.
coverage.supplement: The arXiv version has no separate appendix. Checked the official USENIX presentation page, which links the conference paper, slides and video but no separate experimental supplement; no additional linked experimental supplement located.
coverage.excluded_results: Retain cross-model poisoning as a distinct outcome, not fixed-predictor evasion. Section 4 Equation 13 is a loss-based transferability definition, not a misclassification probability. White-box robustness curves (Figures 3, 5, 10, 14 and 19), gradient similarities/correlations and sensitivity/variance proxies are not additional cross-model error rates. Figures 6, 11, 15 and 20 contain analyses of the corresponding matrices, including target averages and black-box/white-box ratios; these derived summaries are covered by their parent groups, not duplicated as new observations. Figures 9, 18 and 23 show examples, not separately quantified transfer rates. Table 1 reports significance tests, not contingency counts. Same-architecture source/target matrix entries remain in scope because the models use distinct training data.

result_groups.locator: Section 5.1.1; Figure 7 top row, p. 10; Figure 6 derived analyses
result_groups.population: MNIST 8 versus 9; ten independent splits with 5,900 target-training, 5,900 surrogate-training and 1,000 test examples; 20% surrogate-training availability
result_groups.outcome: target test error for ten surrogate by twelve target models at L2 radii 1, 2 and 5
result_groups.evidence: The setup specifies test-set size and attacks both classes; the caption supplies target clean-error reference rows. It does not explicitly state whether all test examples, including target-clean mistakes and source-attack failures, remain in each reported attack denominator. A nominal split size alone is not a filtering rule.

result_groups.outcome: target test error for ten by twelve models at L2 radii 1, 2 and 5

result_groups.evidence: The malware-only evaluation population and operating point are stated, but neither target-clean-correct selection nor successful-source conditioning is explicitly specified. This is not overall clean classification accuracy on all 66,944 test examples.

result_groups.locator: Section 5.1.2; Figure 12 bottom row, p. 13; Figure 11 derived analyses
result_groups.outcome: malware evasion fraction at 0.5% false-positive rate and L1 budgets 5, 10 and 30
result_groups.evidence: Shares the top-row reporting policy. Figure 12 references Figure 7's presentation, but this does not establish retention of target-clean mistakes or source failures, nor a fixed threshold across clean and attacked evaluations.

result_groups.locator: Section 5.2.1, pp. 12-13; Figure 16, p. 14; Figure 15 derived analyses
result_groups.population: MNIST 8 versus 9; 500 training, 1,000 validation and 1,000 separate test examples; ten independent splits
result_groups.outcome: target test error after transferred training-data poisoning, eight surrogate by thirteen target models at 5%, 10% and 20% poisoning
result_groups.evidence: The budget is a fraction of training data, with up to 125 injected points. No target-clean-correct test denominator or source-success restriction is stated. Poisoning changes the learned target and must not be treated as an input perturbation of one fixed target predictor.

result_groups.locator: Section 5.2.2, pp. 13-15; Figure 21, p. 16; Figure 20 derived analyses
result_groups.population: LFW, most common identity versus five others; 300 training, 300 validation and 300 test examples; ten repetitions
result_groups.outcome: target test error after transferred poisoning, eight by thirteen model matrices at 5%, 10% and 20% poisoning
result_groups.evidence: Uses the poisoning protocol with LFW-specific hyperparameters. No explicit target-clean or successful-source denominator restriction is located; absence is unclear rather than no.

f1.evidence: The matrices provide separate target clean-error rows, which are useful positive reporting evidence. Separately trained surrogate models are not the same checkpoints as equally named target models; separate clean results for every surrogate and availability setting could not be established. Malware miss rates must also be distinguished from overall accuracy.

f2.evidence: Dataset/split sizes and test-error terminology are stated, but an explicit denominator rule excluding or retaining target-clean mistakes was not located across the six groups.

f3.evidence: The optimizer returns an attack point, but its algorithm alone does not establish which attempted attacks enter the reported transfer denominator. No explicit retention or exclusion of source-attack failures is stated for the matrices.

f4.evidence: Test sizes are reported, while matrix entries are rounded fractions and results use repeated splits. Multiplying a rounded repeated-run mean by a nominal single-run test size cannot uniquely recover the original numerators and denominators. No matching per-example records were located.

f5.evidence: MNIST evasion explicitly uses numerical L2 radii, on pixels scaled to [0,1]. Drebin explicitly uses L1 feature-insertion budgets, and poisoning reports fractions of injected training data. These are meaningful task-specific budgets, but complete affirmative coverage of the frozen L2/L-infinity field is not established; another norm or a poisoning fraction is not silently converted to an input-space L2/L-infinity radius.

f6.locator: Pinned SecML README, transferability tutorial and PGD-LS implementation
f6.evidence: Accessible SecML code directly cites this paper. Its transfer tutorial trains classifiers on synthetic two-dimensional blobs, not the published MNIST, Drebin or LFW configurations. No original experiment checkpoint/per-example bundle and corresponding evaluator was verified by the bounded search. A generic implementation or newly trained tutorial model does not establish original-result recomputability.

artifact_checks.result: Inspected official presentation listing and arXiv version page. Located conference paper, slides and video; no separate experimental supplement. Searched the paper text for release links and searched the exact title for code.
Search-index snippet points to SecML, but direct retrieval returned 404. The poster was not inspected and is not used as evidence of release sufficiency.

Cloned accessible public library, read README and all source cells of tutorials/04-Transferability.ipynb, inspected attack implementation header and model-zoo loader, and searched paths/references for the paper and transfer experiments. Tutorial cites the paper but uses synthetic blobs and fresh training. Model-zoo loader supports a separate generic registry; no original experiment-specific checkpoint mapping was established. No model code or attack runtime was executed, and library defaults are not attributed to the paper's original implementation.

bounds_checks.reason: The six 10-by-12 matrices contain 720 target-error entries with clean-target reference rows, making this a concrete bounds candidate. However, equality of clean and attacked denominators and absence of source-success selection are not explicit. Do not numerically subtract the reference row until that mapping is established; loss-based Equation 13 and black-box/white-box ratios are not substitutes.

The six matrices supply 720 rates, but the outcome is malware-only evasion at a specified false-positive operating point. A bound would require the same malware cohort and fixed target threshold for baseline and attacked error, plus an unconditional denominator. Do not substitute overall test-set clean error or assume thresholds stayed fixed.

Each dataset supplies three 8-by-13 poisoning matrices (312 entries), but poisoning changes training data and the resulting predictor. The paper's fixed-predictor input-attack identity is not applied without a separately justified estimand and paired outcomes. These results remain in the reporting inventory rather than being dropped from the corpus.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit, not independent recoding or a validated artifact replication.
Preserve the positive target-clean reporting and explicit task-specific budgets despite unresolved paper-level fields.
No numerical bound or PTR/CTR recomputation is added. Source searches are bounded, not proof that no original artifacts exist.
